# RECORD.md

Forager's record of dispatched work, decisions and what happened. Each piece
of work opens with an intent entry, written before anything is built, stating
what will change, where the change stops, what it is expected to do, and when
it counts as finished or abandoned. It closes with exactly one closing entry:
a terminal, or an outcome that carries Closes. Twelve entry types are in use:
intent, terminal, continuation, decision, outcome, observation, finding,
device-note, correction, merge, dispatch-note and handoff. Every entry carries
its Kind, its ID and a Timestamp read from the clock, and ends by saying who
wrote it and on which branch. A decision quotes the owner verbatim and is
recorded once, after any clarifying, not once for every re-ask.

This file is append-only. Nothing already committed is edited or removed; a
correction is a new entry that points at the one it corrects. The one
exception is this header, rewritten on 2026-10-16 at the owner's word
("Update both formats to match current standards"); entry 2026-09-28-1111 quotes the
header it replaced.

What makes an entry well formed is defined in E-GD's RECORDING.md
(github.com/slayer8366/E-GD-Philosophy, branch Test-1), which was written
from this record's own practice. The check_record.py and check_prompts.py
this header used to name were removed from this repository on 2026-09-27,
with the hooks (docs/audits/2026-09-27-kit-hooks-disabled.md). E-GD's
check_record.py implements RECORDING.md for E-GD's own record, but it expects
IDs of the form YYYY-MM-DD-NN, so it is not run here, and entries here are
checked by reading. The existing records in docs/audits/ stay where they are
and are not migrated into this store; docs/audits/README.md indexes them.

Design: docs/process/accountability-design.md. Method: RECORDING.md in E-GD.

**Prediction (outcome — planner):** From the dispatch: 1. At least one variant visibly inverts lightness on Topographical and Street. 2. V2 shifts hue: green towards magenta; V1 largely restores hue (the planner's inference, unverified; the earlier report's claim predicts no inversion at all; either result is evidence). 3. OpenTopoMap's dominant non-background clusters include green vegetation and orange or brown contours or roads; OSM's include green, beige or orange roads and blue water. 4. The phone ends on the non-spike build with every setting restored.
**Prediction (mechanism — coder):** Stated from memory of MapLibre Native's raster fragment shader, not read from the 13.5.0 AAR (unverified): the shader applies hue rotation first (a luma-preserving rotation matrix), then saturation, then contrast, and last maps each channel c to mix(brightness-min, brightness-max, c) = min + (max - min) * c. With min 1 and max 0 that is 1 - c per channel, a full naive RGB invert, not a clamp; the earlier report's "clamp/scale" holds only while min <= max. So (a) V2 inverts lightness and rotates every hue by about 180 degrees: vegetation green goes magenta/purple, pale blue water goes orange-brown, orange contours go blue; (b) V1 rotates hue 180 first, so the invert brings it back roughly to the original hue with lightness inverted; roughly, because MapLibre's hue rotation is a YIQ-style approximation, so some hues and saturations will drift, and pale near-white background becomes near-black; (c) text labels, dark with pale halos in the tiles, become pale with dark halos and stay legible. Risks: if the style parser rejects min > max, the style fails to load and the map is blank (logged by the OnDidFailLoadingMapListener). Separately, because nightModeMaps defaults false (AvailabilityUiState.kt:185) and loads asynchronously (AvailabilityViewModel.kt:854) while the style effect is not keyed on nightMode, a plain relaunch may render day; so each capture forces the style by switching basemap away and back after Night Maps is on. Tile measurement: OpenTopoMap has a pale off-white/cream background with green forest tint, brown contours and blue water lines; OSM in a forest has a large green woodland fill, white/orange/yellow roads, blue water. P50 luminance high (>0.5) on both.
**Finish line:** From the dispatch: steps 1-7 done; the spike reverted on-branch and app/ identical to pre-main at merge; the phone on a non-spike build with its settings restored; findings merged with backup -12; both checkers PASS; both checkouts updated. **Abort conditions:** From the dispatch: a device other than R5CT321008R would be touched; an install needs an uninstall; data would be cleared, created, edited or deleted; the app crashes and does not relaunch; a setting cannot be restored; a tile server returns 403 or 429 (stop fetching; record what exists); an ID collision; a guard or classifier refusal on a repository step, apart from one form-only merge retry in the bare form; CI red; two failed attempts at one step.

Findings doc and its four asset files read. One mismatch with the planner's direction, not with a Base premise: the sample's OSM primary road is beige-orange fad5a3 (as the dispatch's own Measured ground says); pink-red appears as the motorway in the owner's device captures, not in the sample tiles, so "OSM night's pink-red primary roads" is measured against named alternatives and recorded as such.
**Prediction (outcome — planner):** From the dispatch: 1. Every user-mark role has at least one candidate in the purple-magenta band that passes (a) to (e) on Topo in both modes. 2. Street Night's pink-red roads are the closest ground to the magenta end, so some roles pass there with the smallest margin, or fail. 3. The neutral system marks pass easily. 4. At least one pair of user marks collapses under deuteranopia simulation. Lightness and shape are what separate them.
**Prediction (mechanism — coder):** Stated from memory of MapLibre's raster fragment shader (unverified until the source is read): hue-rotate is the spin matrix with weights ((2cos+1)/3, (-sqrt3 sin - cos + 1)/3, (sqrt3 sin - cos + 1)/3), which at 180 degrees is c' = (2/3)(r+g+b) - c per channel, applied to gamma-encoded sRGB; then brightness maps c' to min + (max-min)c' = 1 - c'. Composed, V1 night = clamp(c + 1 - 2m) with m the channel mean: every channel shifts by the same amount, which mirrors the mean about 0.5 and keeps channel differences, hence the hue preservation measured (P90 1 degree). I expect it to reproduce the v1 captures with residual well under 5% of full scale outside labels, puck and anti-aliased edges. Consequences: (i) constraint (b) with the directed casing polarity fails structurally: a white casing against the light day ground cannot reach 3:1 (from the findings' luminances, white vs Topo P50 0.591 is 1.64 and vs P90 0.864 is 1.15; vs OSM 0.570 it is 1.69), and a dark casing at night will fail against the night ground's darkest percentile, since V1 sends the lightest day pixels near black; so every role fails (b) in at least one percentile, by a margin that does not depend on the fill, and the ranking will be decided by the other constraints; (ii) (a) and (e) pass easily in the 300-10 degree band against a 90-150 degree ground; (iii) the binding constraints among user marks are (c) and (d): by day the fill must be dark enough for 3:1 against white (rel. lum at most 0.30), at night light enough against black (at least 0.10), so six user marks plus the dark sighting dot and neutral system marks crowd a narrow band and (d) will be tightest between the dark system marks and the sighting dot; (iv) under deuteranopia/protanopia the magenta band collapses toward blue/grey, so user marks at similar lightness collapse; (v) OSM night's woodland becomes dark mid-green and its beige-orange primary road dark brown-orange, which I expect to be farther from magenta than the planner's pink-red.
**Finish line:** From the dispatch: steps 1-7 done; the board and doc merged with a backup; both checkers PASS; both checkouts updated. Per coder.md item 3 the terminal is written after CI is green and the backup is written, before the merge; the merge and the checkout updates are recorded by the next sweep. Deferral is not provided for.
**Abort conditions:** From the dispatch: a wrong premise; the V1 transform can be neither cited nor fitted to under 5% residual; the PNG exceeds 3 MB after reasonable compression; an ID collision; any guard or classifier refusal, apart from the one form-only merge retry in the bare form; CI red; two failed attempts at one step.

**Prediction (mechanism — coder):** Night Maps does nothing today for two separate reasons, and fixing both is what makes a toggle restyle: the effect is not keyed on nightMode, so it never relaunches on a toggle, and even when it relaunches for another key, AppliedMapStyle has no night component, so needsStyleReload reports no change. With night in both, a toggle on Topographical or Street relaunches the effect, the comparison differs, and setStyle loads the V1 JSON; on Satellite, effective night is false either way, so the relaunch compares equal and nothing reloads. Markers survive every reload because initializeOverlayLayers runs in the setStyle callback and the data effect keys on loadedStyle; I change neither. Cold launch: nightModeMapsLoaded starts false, so the effect returns before requesting any style while the DataStore read is in flight; when the read lands, the flag and the value arrive in one uiState update, the effect relaunches on the flag key and the first style requested is the right one, so no day style is applied first. The map shows MapLibre's blank until then, for as long as one DataStore read takes. Offline: the style loads from its one URL as today; the recolour runs in the setStyle callback before the overlays are added, so the overlays' own line and fill layers are not recoloured. I expect MapLibre to return a literal colour as an rgba() string and colours inside an expression as ["rgba", r, g, b, a] arrays, and I will handle both plus hex and rgb() strings; that is unverified and only a device run shows which form arrives. V1 is linear per channel, night = clamp(c + 255 - 2*mean(r,g,b)), so it keeps HSV hue exactly where no channel clamps, maps black to white and white to black, and matches all 17 swatch-board §3 feature pairs within 1/255 (checked by hand in Python before writing any code: 9 at 1, 8 at 0; one pair, #204FFD, clamps). **The owner, verbatim, in order (2026-10-01):**

- "I just won't explicitly mention that unless asked": the README and the store listing do not describe the app as open source. Code that is public with no licence is not reusable by others, so the description would also be wrong as things stand.

- **Decision 2026-09-28-338's "before release" choice** between a commercial tile provider and the app's own tiles was tied to the sale, as is docs/plans/own-map-tiles.md:22 ("Forager will be sold"). The own-tiles plan itself is not withdrawn by this entry. The policy line -338 quotes names "those that seek donations" beside commercial services, so it applies again if donations are taken while the app still fetches from tile.openstreetmap.org.
- **Attribution** now has to cover the CC BY-NC records as well as the CC BY ones (journal-redesign.md:538 names the CC BY ones).
- **iNaturalist's API and photo terms** (journal-redesign.md:540, "for a commercial app") are still unchecked, now for a free app.
**Checked against "no proprietary software" at e0239399, by the planner:**
- **Read:** every library the app declares (gradle/libs.versions.toml:70-121) and links (app/build.gradle.kts:481-519) is open source: AndroidX, Compose, Room, DataStore, WorkManager, CameraX, Retrofit, OkHttp, kotlinx serialization and coroutines, MapLibre, and mil.nga mgrs. **Open-Meteo's free terms, as a reader returned them on 2026-10-01** from open-meteo.com/en/terms (fetched through a summarising tool, so the quotations are not read from the raw page; no date is shown on it): non-commercial use includes "Using our service for private or non-profit websites or apps that do not have subscriptions or advertising"; commercial use includes "Operating websites or apps that have subscriptions or display advertisements"; "Less than 10'000 API calls per day, 5'000 per hour and 600 per minute". Donations and grants are not mentioned in what was returned. Whether the call limits count per app or per device is not determined.
**Not legal advice, and not settled:** whether a free app that takes donations or grants stays non-commercial under CC BY-NC 4.0, and under Open-Meteo's and OpenStreetMap's terms. The four open questions under the parked companion app (journal-redesign.md:1267-1277) are the same questions and are still open.

**What the owner was told before answering:**
- **Option A:** the recording service holds the return state; the screen messages it and opens a connection to read it back, so a reopened app has a moment of not knowing; that code sits where no automated test reaches.
- **Option B:** one tracker shared by the service and the screen, kept alive and fed by the service; a reopened app reads it at once; nearly all of it testable without a phone; its cost is that two parts of the app write to it at the same time, and eight existing tests move to it one for one.
- **The off-track check today:** three readings about one second apart, more than 25 m gained, so walking cannot trip it and one stray reading can. Arithmetic from the code and the 2026-09-07 walk log's one-second timing; not observed.
**What is decided:**
- **Shape B.**

**The owner's go for the build,** given in the coder's window (read from its message): "Yes, build it".
**The planner's rulings** (appended to the dispatch file): the lookahead is measured (hop + 25 m) along the route from the most recent stored point, which stays within the owner's rulings and adds no number; the arrow stops short of cutting a corner, reusing the existing 10 m self-join distance in a second role, said so in the code and provisional; the route-finding code returns the route's points with its present behaviour unchanged; the shape as the coder proposed.
**Not chosen, and why:** aiming from the last stored point alone, which points backwards often; nearest-point projection, which is against an owner ruling and is put to the owner only if the walk shows the chosen rule is not good enough; a faster write in the recording service, whose batching stays off limits.
**For the owner:** the two disagreements between the route and the off-track alert, and that a stray becomes part of the route home. Both feed plan task T21.

**The coder's stop:** the corner guard as the planner worded it in -418 checked route points from the last stored point onward. Those points are behind a walker who has moved on, so once the walker is more than 10 m past the last stored point the guard pulled the arrow back to that point, pointing it backwards: the very case the lookahead rule of -418 exists to avoid. The coder found it by writing the tests, before any code.
**The planner's correction:** the guard checks only the route points from the walker's assumed place onward, up to the lookahead. The wording in -418 was the planner's error. Its cost is kept visible and tested: a walker standing well to the side of the route is pointed some way up the path. That, and the case where the arrow can still land behind the walker, are for a walk to judge.
**Not chosen:** the guard as first worded; no guard, because the decision record names aiming across a bend as the costly failure on a forest path.

**The walk, 2026-10-03, from the S22's log** (read-only; ~/Zynergy/device-evidence/2026-10-03-owner-walk/PLANNER-READING.md): five off-track alerts, two minutes apart (the cooldown), each a few seconds after a network location reading claiming 400 m accuracy (once 150 m) among GPS readings at about 4 m. The log has no positions, so this is a strong correlation, not a proof. The first fourteen minutes of the recording have no reading lines; why is not determined.
**The owner's account, verbatim:** "1 back towards the start. Only one of those times was when I diverged from the track. The rest was walking on the other side of the street." "2 open, phone off" "3 yes, that one time I diverged was deliberate" "4 nothing felt wrong outside the known issues".
**The owner's choices,** to four questions the planner put, each answered with the planner's recommendation: off track is measured against **"The path I walked"**; **"About 40 m"**, allowing more when GPS reports itself as poor; **"About 15 seconds"** off the path before it alerts; **"Once per stray"**. The planner also told the owner, as not a choice, that rough network readings stop counting, since all five alerts followed one and every app in the research ignores or discounts them.
**The planner's numbers inside those choices, provisional:** the line is 40 m plus the reading's reported accuracy; going off needs 15 s and at least three GPS readings, none back on; re-armed after 10 s back on the path; "the path I walked" is the track as it stood when Return was tapped.
**Change:** dispatch -425 (preserved 2026-10-03-03), opened below. Nothing ships until a replay of the owner's walk shows the new rule alerting at the divergence and not on the other side of the street.

**Kind:** decision
**ID:** 2026-09-28-445
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-03T21:50:00Z
**Decides:** the five decisions of `docs/navigation/2026-10-03-trail-navigation-research.md`
**The owner, verbatim:** "Confirm 1 to 5", to the planner's recommendations:
1. **Data:** OpenStreetMap is the routable base. The public-domain agency trails (Forest Service, BLM, USGS) are a separate reference layer, used to flag gaps, not merged into the route network.
2. **"Not for navigation" sources:** National Park Service and Washington RCO trail data are left out.
3. **Engine:** a spike on the S22 comparing Valhalla and BRouter with real Oregon data before choosing (dispatch -446).
4. **Off-trail behaviour,** as a starting point with every number provisional: off the trail for about 15 s, the map quietly dims the trail, highlights the walker's own track and shows "Off trail · your track leads back", with no sound; no alerts while foraging, and a readout of the way back along their own track; heading back, guidance follows their own track to where they left the trail, with no straight-line shortcut; one gentle alert only when far from both the trail and their track, or near dusk; back on the trail, trail navigation resumes and "Back on trail" shows briefly.
5. **Where it sits:** the next update, alongside the own map tiles (`docs/plans/own-map-tiles.md`) and T7.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch dispatch-439.

The owner did the gestures at the desk while the coder read the log (two-finger input cannot be injected without root); the owner said "As expected", and the log showed no tracking change on pinches or the small nudge, and the drags leaving with "Return to Route".

**Kind:** decision
**ID:** 2026-09-28-509
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-04T19:00:00Z
**Decides:** a round of location work: Forager's own open sensor fusion
**The owner, verbatim:** "I think another run of GPS improvements is due. How much of the phone can we use to actually establish a position? Can the accelerometer or other sensor be used to track movement? Mobile tower signals get weaker when you walk away, and stronger when you walk towards. Can a position be triangulated by detecting these things, and putting it all together into a precise locatoon?" To the planner's answer (GPS for position; steps and compass to carry through gaps and smooth jitter; the barometer for height; cell towers only a rough fallback, hundreds of metres or more in the forest; trail matching as a correction; a fusion filter combining them; Google's fused location excluded as proprietary): "GPS fusion will be useful and I think the real work will pay off, especially keeping it open source."
**Done:** two research agents started by the planner, web only, no patents: pedestrian dead reckoning and its fusion with GNSS, the barometer, battery and pitfalls; and open libraries, Android's raw GNSS measurements and the S22's support, the platform location APIs without Play services, and offline cell positioning (OpenCelliD). Findings go into one report under `docs/navigation/` for the owner. Nothing built.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-167.

**Kind:** finding
**ID:** 2026-09-28-540
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-05T20:15:00Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-539
**Observed:** the owner walked with both phones on 1.0.2763+gbf34fc87 (-516 with main 1d3d2bbb; installed by the -516 coder) and sent screenshots (kept out of the repository; they show street addresses). On both phones, with GPS plainly working (the track recorded point by point along the road), the strip read "Approximate location, finding GPS…" and the HUD "Approximate, finding GPS…" with a network-sized circle; on the S22, once away from Wi-Fi, the HUD read "No fix for 249 min" while its coordinates and the blue dot kept moving.
**Read by the planner over adb, read only:** both phones' clocks are about 4 h 09 min ahead of real time (S22 and S26 at 2026-10-06T00:10Z when the laptop and GitHub's Date header both read 2026-10-05T20:00Z), and both have automatic time off (`settings get global auto_time` = 0). Neither the -516 report nor its commits mention setting a clock.
**The planner's diagnosis, inferred, not yet confirmed by logs:** a GPS fix carries satellite time; the app judges freshness against the phone's wall clock (`LocationFix.Update.ageMillis`, `domain/LocationTracker.kt`; ten callers). With the wall clock 249 min ahead, every GPS fix reads as 249 min old, so lost (5 min and over): the display falls back to the newest network reading, stamped by the phone's own clock and so fresh, which -510 shows as approximate; with no network reading (the S22 off Wi-Fi), "No fix for 249 min". The track is unaffected (the sampler does not judge age). The same clock drives the sundown countdown and alerts, so on these phones they would fire against the wrong time.
**Why it matters beyond the test:** a phone whose clock is wrong (set by hand, or a phone without a SIM that never syncs) loses every precise position the app shows, with GPS working. The platform offers a clock that cannot be set by hand (`Location.getElapsedRealtimeNanos` against `SystemClock.elapsedRealtime`), which the app already uses elsewhere (`ui/log/CameraAbsence.kt:47`). This is the "phone's clock" row -519's fallback table did not yet have.
**Open for the owner:** who set the clocks and why; whether to set them back (not done by the planner); and a fix, to be dispatched after a log confirms the diagnosis.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173.

**Confirmed (2026-10-05T20:31Z, read only):** each phone's newest `ForagerFix` GPS line, logged moments before, carries `time=` 249 min (S22) and 250 min (S26) behind that phone's own clock (`adb shell date +%s%3N`). The diagnosis in -540 holds: GPS is fine; the phones' clocks are wrong, and the app measures a fix's age against them.

**Kind:** continuation
**ID:** 2026-09-28-542
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-05T20:50:00Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-541
**The planner's answer to the drawbacks question,** in brief: ageing a live fix on the phone's since-boot clock (Location's elapsed-realtime stamp) makes freshness immune to any wall-clock change. Its limits: it works only within one power-on, so stored things (the platform's last known position, track points) keep the wall clock; the sundown alerts still follow the phone's clock (correcting them from GPS time is a separate, larger decision with no data asking for it); a fix without the stamp falls back to wall-clock age, logged; the tests gain a second time per fix; a saved track's start (phone clock) and points (satellite time) still disagree when the clock is wrong. The premise "an hour outside network range is an hour of uncalibrated clock" was corrected: drift is about a second a day, and the 249 min of -540 was a manual change.
**The owner, verbatim:** "I'd like to go on a few more walks before deciding that."
**So:** no dispatch. The since-boot clock question waits for more walks, with the EKF's four questions (-538).
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173.

If the bar's text can't stay readable at the strip's height at large fonts, the coder reports that rather than growing the strip.

**Title:** launch-verifyerror: URGENT, main crashes on launch (ART VerifyError in CompactMapTab)
**Dispatch-file:** preserved/2026-10-08-04.md
**Context:** the owner, verbatim: "App force closes when trying to start". The connected S22 still had 1.0.2874 (no crash). The owner plugged in the S26, which has 1.0.3086+g0e766d94, installed 11:36 PDT. Its crash buffer shows java.lang.VerifyError rejecting AvailabilityCompactMapUiKt: CompactMapTab (about 77 parameters plus ten int masks) fails ART verification ("register v0 has type Reference: …MapMode but expected Integer"). Robolectric and CI never run ART's verifier, so every suite was green. The planner paused T6b again (PAUSE file), as the owner chose for the earlier fix ("Pause T6b, build, resume (Recommended)"). Nothing was installed on the S26; it was read only. The fix: reproduce on the S22 with install -r, shrink CompactMapTab's parameters into holder classes with no behaviour change, verify on the S22, and add a guard against a repeat.
**Sent:** to a coder subagent, urgent.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -740.

**Kind:** continuation
**ID:** 2026-09-28-740
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-08T18:50:52Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-739
**Cause confirmed; #203 to be reverted.** The owner asked, verbatim: "Is it better if main is fixed first? You're the planner so let me know what makes it better". The planner recommended confirming the cause with CI's own APKs, then reverting #203 so main launches while the proper fix is built. The owner, verbatim: "Confirm and undo, leave S26". On the S22, CI's debug APK for f8739856 (before #203, 1.0.3072) opens with no VerifyError, and 0e766d94 (1.0.3086) crashes. The coder's dex reading: CompactMapTab has 246 registers at f8739856 against 259 at 0e766d94. #203's two added parameters pushed the method past 256 registers, and at 0x10E D8's code reads v0 (holding mapMode) where it should have moved v256: a D8 register-allocation miscompile. The planner opened a revert PR (branch revert-203, git revert -m 1 0e766d94), to merge on green CI. The S26 is left alone. The fix (-739) brings the join back with grouped parameters (67 to 37).
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -741.

**Kind:** continuation
**ID:** 2026-09-28-741
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-08T19:00:34Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-739, 2026-09-28-740
**The fix plan, and an S22 launch guard.** The coder's first fix (CompactMapTab's parameters grouped from 67 to 37, 249 registers) still crashed on the S22, with a different VerifyError in the same method ("[0x1E20] copy-reference v12<-v197 type=BooleanConstant"). So the 256-register explanation was incomplete. D8 9.3.16, bundled with AGP 9.3.1, miscompiles this one very large method (about 12,000 dex code units, 222 JVM locals, 106 inlined calls including 51 remembers). The JVM bytecode is correct, which is why Robolectric and CI are green. No public R8 fix matches. AvailabilityScreen (401 registers), CompactMainScaffold (385) and JournalTab (289) are also large and verify today. No offline ART verifier exists. The owner, verbatim: "Try newer tool, then split (Recommended)": first a one-build test of a newer pinned R8 (9.3.31) on the S22, then, either way, split CompactMapTab's body into smaller composables with no behaviour change, and then the landscape join returns. And: "S22 launch check before merging (Recommended)": before merging any change to screens, the build is installed on the S22 (install -r), checked with cmd package compile -m verify, and launched once.

**Timestamp:** 2026-10-09T17:36:15Z
**Title:** The forecast model starts lean on input layers (forager-forecast D121)
**Context:** The owner asked: "How many layers should be used? To me it seems like the sighting chances just increase with more data added, but maybe I'm not seeing the logic." The planner explained four things: a calibrated chance is sharpened, not raised, by data; the limit is the roughly 1,200 Cantharellus records; layers overlap; and effort measures people. The plan already requires layers to earn their place on held-out years. The planner recommended a lean start of about 6 to 10 inputs.
**Decision:** The owner, verbatim: "Go with the lean start". Habitat: host trees, soil pH, the land and water mask. Trigger: a few weather measures (recent rain, soil moisture, temperature). Observation: effort. Anything further enters only if it beats the model without it on held-out years (D33). Written as D121 on forager-forecast branch d121-lean-start (from t6b-continental-layers), pushed, unmerged. Its merge follows the repo's rules (D40).

A read-only agent pulled both phones' databases with run-as cat (nothing changed on either phone; raw files and scripts in ~/Zynergy/device-evidence/2026-10-09-l3-tracks/, outside every repo; no coordinates printed). Track S22 6f6b7c03 (517 points), S26 fcd35b03 (532 points), both starting 13:09:45 PDT (-795's start time is right for both).
**Read from data:** both loops close within 9 m (S22) and 7 m (S26); lengths 3,669 m and 3,408 m. Every gap over 30 s on both phones moved 5 to 15 m and lines up with the owner's stops. The S22 kept 85 points in its screen-off window 13:48:37 to 13:57:10 (the recording did not stall; consistent with -797). Way back vs way out: S22 median 7.3 m, p90 19.3 m; S26 median 4.4 m, p90 11.1 m. Two-phone separation over 471 matched points: median 12.1 m, p90 20.4 m, max 59.7 m; only 51% within the two phones' reported accuracies combined. **Inferred:** 14:03:05 to 14:04:10 is an S22 error: it fell up to 60 m behind the S26 while reporting 3.8 to 7.5 m accuracy, then caught up 98 m in 25 s; the S26 was smooth. 13:57:46 to 13:58:25 is probably real movement: both phones left the way-out path by 58 to 82 m together and both off-track alerts fired within 5 s (13:57:48 S22, 13:57:53 S26); a shared canopy error is not ruled out; the owner is asked. Unexamined: a 37 m separation at 13:40:53 to 13:41:01.

**Kind:** decision
**ID:** 2026-09-28-901
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-12T00:46:56Z
**Title:** The page explains the percentage against the average week, before Monday; a wider fit after Monday (owner)
**Context:** The owner, after opening the live page on a phone (screenshots kept off GitHub): "The sighting chance zone covers such a small area compared to the rest. Plus the highest sighting chance is 12% when I know chanterelles are out there in full force right now". The planner explained: the pilot's fit box is T1's 42.0 to 49.5 N, 125.0 to 121.0 W (t1_design.py:35; D123), while weather was pulled for 40.0 to 49.5 N, 125.0 to 111.0 W. Sighting chance is D11's "the chance the group is reported in a weather cell and week, given at least one fungal observation of any kind there that week". 1,138 of 52,718 tested cell-weeks (2.16%) had a chanterelle report, so 12% is about 5 to 6 times the average.
**Rulings (owner, verbatim answers):** "Yes, before Monday (Recommended)": tapping a cell adds one plain comparison line, and the legend shows the same comparison, from the model's own test data, via a new manifest field. "Plan a wider fit after Monday (Recommended)": a fit and review over the whole area the map shows, with the same honest test, after the meeting.
**Planner's wording, refined from the example the owner chose ("About 5 times a typical week (a typical week is about 2%).") because the 2% is an all-season average:** ratio = chance ÷ base rate (positives ÷ units over the all-years test, 1,138 ÷ 52,718). At 1.5 or more: "About N times the average week across the year (about 2%)." with N rounded to a whole number. From 0.67 to under 1.5: "About the same as the average week across the year (about 2%)." Under 0.67: "Below the average week across the year (about 2%)." Legend: "Average week across the year: about 2%." The owner is told of the refinement.
**What it sets:** the scorer adds base_rate (positives, units, rate, source) to the manifest and republishes, cells unchanged. The site coder shows the line and the legend note. Checks run on a preview; the merge waits for the owner's word tonight.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -902.

- Then: "A, and allow the user to select multiple finds, and they can be added to a queue, while the user goes through and edits/confirms their find, then it moves to the next one. Offer to send GPS location to each find".
- Then: "Start with on. Offer each time" and "They can select from the map > open in journal > share to iNaturalist".
**What it sets:**
- **Near term, in Forager:**
  1. Select several finds in the Journal, or reach one from the map through "Open in journal".
  2. Tap "Share to iNaturalist".
  3. For each find in turn, review and edit it (edits save to the journal), with "Include location" on to start, offered each time.
  4. Confirm hands its photos (and location, if included) to iNaturalist's app.
  5. Coming back moves to the next find. A find can be skipped, or the queue stopped.
  6. Sent finds show "Sent to iNaturalist", not "posted", since Forager can't see whether posting finished.
- **Later:** a companion app takes over uploading, alongside the identification system.
- **Unchanged:** the no-identification rule. A share carries only the user's own ID, or none.
**Next:** a read-only check of iNaturalist's app (dispatch 2026-10-13-01) before any spec: does it accept shared photos, several at once, and read their location?
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. The check is recorded by this entry; it builds nothing. Next free ID -964.

**Context:** the read-only check (dispatch 2026-10-13-01, the coder's report) found:
- iNaturalist's Play app (org.inaturalist.android) takes a find's shared photos as one observation, up to 20 (ObservationEditor.java:3482-3540);
- it reads GPS and its accuracy from the first photo's EXIF, without filling the current position;
- it reads the date from EXIF and blanks it when none is found (:3800-3853);
- it accepts no documented name or notes, only an undocumented species_guess extra (:1062);
- after saving, it calls finishAndRemoveTask (ObservationListActivity.java:813-815), which would close a task Forager launched it into;
- it blocks some sharing apps over stripped metadata (issue #811);
- a replacement app is in closed testing and treats multiple shared photos as separate observations.
Forager's camera scrub removes the date with the location (PhotoMetadataScrub.kt:56).
**The owner, verbatim:** asked whether to pre-fill the user's own identification through the undocumented extra: "A - skip it".
**What it sets:**
- **The owner's ruling:** no name or identification goes with a share.
- **The planner's calls, for the owner to correct:**
  - share copies always carry the find's date and time, and GPS and accuracy only with "Include location" on; the originals are never changed;
  - iNaturalist opens in its own task, and the queue position is saved;
  - a new "Sent to iNaturalist" state records the date sent, and re-sharing a sent find says so first;
  - with iNaturalist not installed, the button says so and offers its Play page.
- **The spec:** docs/plans/inaturalist-share-queue.md on branch inat-share-spec, for the owner's review. Not dispatched.

**Kind:** decision
**ID:** 2026-09-28-974
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-14T03:55:28Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-973
**Title:** RAW capture design: a format chip (JPG default, HEIF, PNG, TIF, RAW, RAW+), an HDR chip, aligned bursts, only the final photo kept (owner)
**The owner, verbatim:**
- "1 A, like phones do already" (burst frames aligned in software, so handheld works);
- "2 no, only keep the final product";
- "3 yes sounds good. That outputs a processed RAW (RAW+). Users can choose other formats, and the final output will be the chosen format. It will still go through RAW processing like frame averaging, HDR burst (if HDR mode is chosen) and debayering, until RAW mode is selected where it outputs an unprocessed RAW."
- Then: "1 the usual form" (RAW+ is a linear DNG), "3 JPG selected by default", "2 JPG, HEIF, PNG, TIF, RAW, RAW+", "4 yes" (HDR is its own chip).
**What it sets:**
- **Format chip:** on the camera strip, offering JPG (default), HEIF, PNG, TIF, RAW+ and RAW.
- **HDR chip:** a separate chip, off or on.
- **Every format except RAW:** a RAW burst is aligned in software, averaged in floating point, HDR-merged when HDR is on, and debayered. One final photo is saved in the chosen format. RAW+ is a linear DNG: processed and debayered, but unedited.
- **RAW:** one unprocessed sensor DNG, with no averaging, HDR or debayering.
- **Only the final file is kept;** burst frames are discarded.
- **On phones without RAW support,** the RAW chips don't appear and capture works as today.
- **Planner's call:** formats the journal can't show (DNG, TIF, possibly HEIF and PNG) also get a small preview image for the journal and viewer.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Still open: DNG and TIF privacy (make, model and time; the scrub is JPEG-only), adopting the experimental Camera2Interop for manual exposure, and per-format storage size. Next free ID -975.

Then, after the planner described the two behaviours and Android 17's large-screen rule: "I never asked the lock to be removed. I only wanted the keep in portrait feature removed. The camera is to remain as is. This is a bug, so fix it".
**What it sets:**

**Context:** the coder's plan (base 94a10cc3, read from the pinned CameraX 1.6.2 AARs) found:
- RAW and RAW+JPEG come from one check in 1.6.2, so they can't differ;
- CameraX reports "no RAW", with no "unknown", when its CameraInfo isn't the internal type;
- Camera2CameraInfo needs the ExperimentalCamera2Interop opt-in, which only lint enforces, and CI runs no lint;
- the platform has no HEIF or TIFF bitmap encoder (PNG yes, DNG via DngCreator);
- the app binds the front camera only when there is no back camera.
**What it sets (planner's calls):**
- a new data-layer reader file;
- camera reads at bind, and the encoder probe once per process in the background;
- the unbound front camera and the back camera's physical cameras also probed and logged;
- PNG measured by a real 1×1 compress;
- a CameraX "no" with Camera2 unreadable is Unknown;
- one revert check per rule group;
- no UI change, held by a positive control.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Branch raw-stage1-probe. Next free ID -996.

**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1008
**Title:** Forager writes the RAW file itself from stage 2; its processing is geared to nature photography (owner)
**The owner, verbatim:** first, "We should assume control of the pipeline. Phones do a good job in taking photos, but the quality is dependent on software, which is calibrated from phone to phone. A unified software approach through the app will help ensure similar (aside pixel size, count, style, etc.) photo quality can be taken from different phones. That's why I wrote debayering for OSCam and the whole process". Then, offered A (the phone's writer, cleaned afterwards, uncompressed) or B (Forager writes the DNG from the sensor data, losslessly compressed, nothing in it but what Forager writes): "Let Forager write it. We can gear the processing towards nature photography, whereas phones in general are geared for selfies and city elements".
**What it sets:** from stage 2 on, Forager owns the RAW pipeline: it takes the sensor data from the camera and writes the DNG with its own code, with lossless compression (-975) and no location, make, model or time (-975, -1008). Later processing stages (debayering, averaging, HDR) are Forager's own, tuned for nature subjects rather than the phone's defaults. If the camera library can't hand over the sensor data this way, the planner tells the owner before anything is built on the fallback (the phone's writer).
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -1010.

**Kind:** outcome
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1067
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-15T22:22:06Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1065
**Title:** Unbinned RAW bounds: on the S22 the full-resolution route is blocked by the maker's camera driver; Forager's RAW is the sensor's 9-in-1 binned mode
**Observed:** prompts/preserved/2026-10-15-10-unbinned-raw-bounds.md (read only; S22 getprop, pm list packages, dumpsys package on three of the maker's camera packages; the earlier dumpsys re-read; the S26 not attached, its section unverified). Binning READ: the sensor-name tag names a 108 MP 3x3-cell sensor whose maker's launch material describes 9-to-1 binning to 12 MP. The block: every camera's driver interface is version 3.5; the platform's full-resolution features need 3.7, and the camera service drops the full-resolution setting for older drivers (read in the platform source); the driver dates from Android 12 and is unchanged through Android 16. "Binning factor used: FALSE" only means a standard colour layout, not unbinned data. Routes: the platform's full-resolution mode and the native cell-pattern route are not offered on the S22; the maker's hidden tables list a 12000x9000 RAW stream an app might request by vendor setting names (undetermined whether the driver delivers it to Forager; fragile; 135 to 216 MB a frame; probably re-arranged by the phone); the maker's partner SDK is an agreement, not public; the maker's own RAW app is closed and its RAW colour-processed. Physics: a full-resolution RAW from these sensors is either the untouched 3x3 pattern (no store-app route found) or a re-arranged (processed) one; at the same output size it is never less noisy; its only gain is detail in good light. Workarounds: keep the binned RAW and describe it truthfully; burst merging of hand-shake-shifted binned frames for extra detail (Wronski et al. 2019), built on the averaging burst; a dev-only experiment on the S22's hidden setting; a read-only look at the S26's tables.
**For the owner:** pure (binned) against detail (re-arranged); a merged burst as the detail version with raw frames as the pure one; the dev experiment on the hidden setting; the S26 read-only look.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -1068.

**Timestamp:** 2026-10-15T23:08:28Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1063
**Title:** Fast-burst test on the S22: platform RAW bursts at 30 frames a second (8 frames in 233 ms); swap and hand-back measured; the phone's noise-reduction, hot-pixel and shading modes leave the RAW unchanged
**Build:** PR #230 (raw-stage3-platform-burst, head 403d71be; CI 38818478822: 5,101 tests, 0 failures, 24 skipped; tests first, run 38816813305, 29 failures from stubs; four revert checks per the coder; all paths under app/src/debug or testDebug, no @Ignore). dev backed up (dev-20261015T230404Z-7a2c0286.bundle) and the PR rebase-merged by the planner: 3ff702ea, 5ac4c4c2, 63f7c6e0. APK 1.0.3371+g93be8eb5 installed on the S22 with adb install -r.
**Device run (session 1, ~16:05 PDT, indoor, phone on the desk):** log and 32 DNGs (183 MB) kept off GitHub at ~/Zynergy/device-evidence/2026-10-15-stage3-platform-s22/. Borrow: CameraX CLOSED at 102 ms, platform device opened at 519 ms, session (PRIV 1440x1080 + RAW 4000x3000) configured at 754 ms; AE and AWB converged at 2,661 ms and locked at 2,898 ms, so the first RAW frame came at 3,106 ms after the trigger, the wait being convergence in a fresh session. All four runs (default locked; NR and hot pixel OFF; manual exposure at the converged 1/60 s, ISO 223; shading OFF): 8 of 8 frames by captureBurst, sensor timestamps exactly 33.33 ms apart (30.0 frames a second), 233 ms first to last frame, 8 of 8 DNGs written through ForagerDngWriter; heap peak 112 MB of 268 MB. Hand-back: platform closed, CameraX OPEN 571 ms and the viewfinder STREAMING 716 ms after hand-back began; the dialog's chip still read RAW.
**Processing modes:** by default the still template reports noise reduction, hot pixel, shading, edge and tonemap all HIGH_QUALITY; the NR-off run reports NR and hot pixel OFF, the shading run shading OFF. **Planner's measurement:** after removing each frame's overall brightness (spread under 0.07%) and keeping fine-scale differences (a 5x5 high-pass) in low-texture areas, the temporal noise variance is the same in every run (green 7.15 default, 7.18 NR off, 7.29 manual, 7.23 shading off; red 8.22 to 8.32) and neighbouring residuals are uncorrelated (about -0.03, the high-pass's own small bias). So on the S22 those modes change nothing in the RAW data: its RAW is not noise-reduced or hot-pixel-corrected by the phone. (A first pass without the high-pass read correlations of 0.6 to 0.9, from low-frequency frame-to-frame change, not noise; it is not cited.)
**Not yet measured:** the S26; a tripod and outdoor light; the swap with CameraX's exposure handed to manual settings (which would remove most of the 2.6 s wait; the manual run shows manual exposure works).
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. dev now carries the dev-tools commit and six probe commits above main cb25b582; main has since moved to 402489ae (documents only); dev's rebase is now unblocked. Next free ID -1070.

**Kind:** decision
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1086
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-16T12:24:32Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1085
**Title:** Main is the production branch: it changes only by a promotion from pre-main, after CI, phone checks, the UX auditor's report and the owner's approval for public use. Small tasks and large features go into pre-main; experiments and long research go on dev, which becomes pre-main plus the dev tools (owner)
**The owner, verbatim:** "Main is the sacred live production branch where all Play builds come from. So anything going into main from this point (not retroactive on already running coders), has to be tested, debugged, and approved for public use", and "use pre-main as the working branch for non extensive tasks" (in full in -1085). On dev: "Dev branch is for experimental tasks and research that takes a while. For example, the camera work is currently being handled there". To the planner's follow-up questions: large non-experimental features: "Own branch, into pre-main (Recommended)"; an experiment chosen to ship: "Carried to pre-main (Recommended)"; the dev build: "Pre-main + experiments (Recommended)"; messaging the old planner window: "Yes, message it (Recommended)". From -1085: urgent fixes: "Same gate, front of queue (Recommended)"; the auditor's verdict: "Advises, you decide (Recommended)".
**What it sets, for Forager from now on:**
(1) **Main** is the production branch, and every Play build comes from it. It changes only by a promotion pull request from pre-main. A promotion passes four things in order: CI green on pre-main; a device check of a plain pre-main build (no dev tools) on the S22 Ultra and the S26 Ultra, and on the tablet when screens change, with bugs found fixed on pre-main first; the UX auditor's report against Forager's QA philosophy (the auditor advises: pass, pass with items, or fail); and the owner's approval for public use. Then the merge. A promotion that changes no app code has no device check. Documents count: nothing goes into main except by a promotion.
(2) **Pre-main** is the working branch. Small tasks merge into it directly. A large feature that is not experimental (for example trail navigation) is built on its own branch and merged into pre-main when done.
(3) **Dev** holds experiments and long research (the camera work now). It is pre-main plus the dev-tools commit (-930) plus the experiments, rebased after every pre-main update, so the owner's phone runs what is next for release. Dev is never merged into main or pre-main. An experiment chosen to ship is carried onto pre-main without dev tools, then promoted through the gate.

**Kind:** decision
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1103
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-16T17:49:26Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1083, 2026-09-28-1102
**Title:** The lens chooser's design: real-lens buttons only, labelled by zoom number, above the shutter; the chosen lens remembered while the app is open; a lens without RAW keeps its button and saves a JPG with a line saying so (owner)
**The owner, verbatim:** to four questions, each answered with the planner's recommendation: "Lens buttons only (Recommended)"; "Zoom numbers (Recommended)"; "Remember while app is open (Recommended)"; "Keep it; save a JPG and say so (Recommended)". Preceded by "Yes start there" (design the lens chooser first, -1102).
**Prior art (planner's check, web, 2026-10-16):** phone makers' camera apps and the other major platform's camera put a row of zoom-number buttons above the shutter, the active one highlighted, with a tap to switch and a hold or drag for a fine zoom wheel, and pinch zoom on the picture. RAW apps often allow RAW on some lenses only, depending on the phone; one documented case is an ultra-wide that couldn't save RAW. Followed: the placement, the zoom-number labels, tap to switch. Departed from, by the owner's choice: no pinch and no zoom wheel (each button is a real lens at full quality; RAW cannot be cropped). Departed from, by Forager's own rule: phone camera apps reset to 1x on every open, but Forager remembers the lens while the app is open (CLAUDE.md, "UX defaults"; as the format chip, -1005) and returns to 1 after a restart.
**What it sets (design, the step path shown to the owner):** opening the camera shows a row of the phone's real back lenses above the shutter, centred, labelled by measured zoom (S26: .6, 1, 3, 5; S22: .6, 1, 3, 10), on 1 the first time. Tap 3, and the picture jumps to the 3x lens with 3 highlighted; take the photo, and it is saved from that lens, RAW included. Tap 1 to go back. The row stays put and its labels turn with the phone, like the other icons (the camera never rotates, -980, -981). A lens that can't give RAW on some phone, with RAW chosen, keeps its button and saves a JPG with the line "This lens can't save RAW, saved as JPG." (wording to be confirmed with the owner before build). Built on engine A (-1102), which can pick each physical lens (-1095, -1101).
**Not authorised by this:** any build. Open, for later: averaging bursts on lenses other than the main (stage 3); the exact copy of the no-RAW line.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -1104.

**Kind:** outcome
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1106
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-16T20:23:30Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1105
**Corrects:** 2026-09-28-1104, its premise that editors honouring the DNG crop tags "open it cropped, and the full frame stays recoverable"
**Title:** Lens chooser, Phase 1: the build is feasible, but three premises fail (the RAW crop tags, the telephotos' JPG size, a picture blank of about half a second on each lens switch); the planner's camera-table read settles the coder's open facts
**Report-file:** preserved/2026-10-16-04-phase1-report.md (filed unedited)
**Coder's findings (read, with file and line in the report):**
- ForagerDngWriter writes no crop tags.
- The DNG specification's DefaultCrop is for edge margins, and DefaultUserCrop (DNG 1.4) is the user's crop. darktable hard-cuts DefaultCrop, so the full frame can't be recovered there, and it offers DefaultUserCrop only as a crop the user can switch on. LibRaw applies neither unless the app asks, and ignores crops tighter than 0.55. RawTherapee ignores both. Adobe's editor is unverified.
- A lens switch means a new camera session: estimated 0.45 to 0.55 s of frozen picture on the S26 and about 0.8 s on the S22.
- The pinch floor is 0.58x.
- The lens memory can be a process-wide object in the debug build.
- The row must not move when the message line above the shutter grows.
- DngContract.kt needs the planner's approval to change.
**Planner's read (adb shell dumpsys media.camera on the S22, saved to ~/Zynergy/device-evidence/2026-10-16-camera-tables-s22/; the S26 from 2026-10-15's saved tables):**
- Minimum focus distance: the main wide 10 cm (10 diopters) on both phones; the 3x telephoto 40 cm (2.5); the S26's 5x and the S22's 10x 80 cm (1.25).
- Largest JPG: S22 cameras 6 and 7, 3648x2736; S26 camera 6, 3648x2736; S26 camera 7, 4080x3060.
- Crop region is a per-lens request key on the S22 (cropRegion and zoomRatio among availablePhysicalCameraRequestKeys). Not found in the first such listing on the S26, so the S26 is undetermined.
**Planner's calls (technical, stated to the owner):**
- DngContract.kt may gain a nullable crop field, null by default, in a dev-only commit.
- The lens memory is a process-wide object, so it is kept while the app's process lives, including after backing out and returning.
- The row sits in a fixed place directly above the shutter, with the message line above the row, so the row never moves.
**For the owner:** the RAW crop note; JPG size on 3648x2736 lenses; what happens during a lens switch; close focus with the telephotos.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -1107.

**Kind:** decision
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1107
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-16T20:33:14Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1106
**Supersedes:** 2026-09-28-1104's RAW crop wording ("editors that honour them open it cropped and the full frame stays recoverable") and its JPG size for the 3648x2736 lenses
**Title:** Lens chooser after Phase 1: the RAW carries a hard crop (DNG DefaultCrop); JPGs are saved at the lens's own size; on a lens switch the picture holds and the shutter waits; too close for the telephoto, the main lens is used zoomed (owner)
**The owner, verbatim:** to four questions: "Hard crop" (the planner had recommended the suggested crop, DefaultUserCrop); "Lens's own size (Recommended)"; "Hold last picture, shutter waits (Recommended)"; "Use the main lens, zoomed (Recommended)".
**What it sets:**
- **The RAW crop.** A zoomed RAW keeps the lens's whole untouched mosaic in the file, with DefaultCropOrigin and DefaultCropSize set to the zoom. As stated to the owner: darktable opens it zoomed and can't recover the rest there, while LibRaw-based apps (unless they opt in) and RawTherapee ignore it. Adobe's editor is unverified. This departs from the DNG specification's stated use of DefaultCrop (edge margins); the alternative, DefaultUserCrop, was considered and not chosen. The mosaic itself is never cut, so -1056's real RAW holds.
- **JPG size.** A JPG is saved at the chosen lens's own full size, enlarged by the camera from any crop: 4000x3000 on the main and ultra-wide lenses and the S26's 5x (4080x3060 lens), and 3648x2736 on the 3x lenses and the S22's 10x. There is no software re-encode. -1104's "the usual 4000x3000" is narrowed to "the lens's own full size".
- **Lens switch.** The picture holds its last frame; the new lens's button lights at once; a shutter press waits until the new lens is streaming.
- **Close focus.** When the subject is closer than the chosen telephoto can focus (3x: 40 cm; the S26's 5x and the S22's 10x: 80 cm), the main lens is used, cropped to the zoom, and its button lights.
**Planner's calls stand (-1106):** DngContract.kt gains a nullable crop field, in a dev-only commit; the lens memory is process-wide; the row is fixed directly above the shutter, with messages above it.
**Next:** the planner gives the coder Phase 2's go (dispatch 2026-10-16-04).
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -1108.

**Report-file:** forager-forecast docs/audits/2026-10-16-t7-fit-report.md on t7-build (b5c3d26, pushed). **Observed (the planner read the report's Verdict and caveats sections at b5c3d26):**
- **The fit.** 14.2 h at 41f9c79, finished 2026-10-17T02:07:48Z. 15,624 presences against 500,000 background points.
- **Pooled held-out AUC.** Full 0.88146; A (effort only) 0.87728; B (effort plus forest) 0.87880.
- **Against the bar (D140), with weather-cell-clustered 95% intervals.** Full minus A +0.00419 (+0.00211 to +0.00629); full minus B +0.00266 (+0.00100 to +0.00423). The forested blocks are similar. The bar is met.
- **Reported beside it, with no verdict:**
  - Effort alone carries almost all of it: every habitat input together adds 0.004.
  - Block-clustered intervals include zero in all four comparisons.
  - Block by block it is a split: the full model is above A in 7 of 14 informative blocks.
  - At level I it loses in Marine West Coast Forests, which hold 8,958 of the presences.
  - The comparison group (Laetiporus, wood rot) gains +0.0232 over A from the same inputs, and its map's rank correlation with the mycorrhizal map is 0.230, so the gain is not shown to be mycorrhizal-specific.
  - The licence track does not pass B.
  - Tuning chose the most regularised configuration in every fold.
- **Nothing published, shown or viewed;** the rasters and mask map were never opened. There is no D18 review, and CI was not run on t7-build.
**The planner's flag for the review (-1108):** the weighting fix 41f9c79 was made after the smoke run's P10 "fail" (fit.log, 2026-10-16T11:43:32Z), and the full run then "pass"ed. The fix was mechanical (no split was possible) and was test-first, but the reviewer must confirm it stands independently of the verdict.
**Coder's readings beyond the plan:** the add-one bands reuse the base model's configurations; the 30-presence rule is applied to fitted presences; the licence track drops cells without CC0/CC BY effort; the under-minimum blocks were read as D139's "uninformative", not a halt; and the verify report's "25 level III blocks" is in fact 26.
**Next, under -1108:** the bar is cleared, so the independent review runs before anything is published. Brought to the owner with these caveats first.

**Prediction (mechanism, coder):** the S22's camera service passes a per-lens crop region to the HAL without converting it, and the HAL frames physical streams from zoom ratio, so the crop is ignored. **Kind:** continuation
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1217
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-18T01:07:35Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1216
**Title:** The tablet camera restart: Hazel's Phase 1 mechanism, accepted by the planner
**Prediction (mechanism, coder):**
- **The cause:** CameraXCaptureSession.kt:831's `DisposableEffect(view, held)` is keyed on the hold flag. That flag is false at ROTATION_0 and true at 90, 180 and 270 (NaturalOrientationHold.kt:65, :107-113). So each turn into or out of 0 detaches and re-attaches the surface provider and switches the viewfinder between SurfaceView (PERFORMANCE) and TextureView (COMPATIBLE), and that rebuilds the camera session.
- **Not a rebind:** bindToLifecycle is not re-called (InAppCameraDialog.kt:198's keys don't change).
- **The log agrees:** 8 turns touching 0 and 8 CLOSING lines; 7 turns among 1, 2 and 3 and none.
- **The fix:** key on "can be held", meaning held, or full screen with smallestScreenWidthDp ≥ 600, so on a full-screen tablet the viewfinder stays COMPATIBLE at all four rotations. Phones and split screen are unchanged.
**The planner's acceptances:**
- the 600 dp threshold;
- a test seam counting surface-provider attachments.
**Added by the planner:**
- the device check must show the picture at ROTATION_0 unchanged now that the tablet runs COMPATIBLE there;
- an unfolded foldable would also always run COMPATIBLE, untested, to be stated;
- a revert check on the key change itself.
The planner's own inference in the dispatch (a size change triggering a rebind) was half wrong: it is a key change, not the window size.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. Next free ID -1218.

- **Should-fix:**
  - the selection caveat belongs in the verdict table;
  - fit.log should print condition 2's block interval;
  - 23 of the 99 specimen genera have no platform presence;
  - condition 4's background should be drawn per collecting station;

  - road distance alone ranks within-cell pairs at 0.654.

  - strengthening won't change the verdict (worth running for the record: nested selection and per-station condition 4);
  - stop T7 for the PNW? Yes, as posed. Keep the record, with the per-genus and within-block signals as leads.

**The owner, verbatim:** "Yes", to "do you want the quick change that takes the Pi out of serving now?". Also: "Thats the brandonlee1 account", confirming forager-pmtiles' account.
**What it sets:**
- **The change:** the owner deletes `PI_ORIGIN_URL` from forager-pmtiles' variables in the Cloudflare dashboard and deploys. With it unset, `fetchFromPi` returns at once and every tile is served from R2 (`server/pmtiles-worker/src/index.ts:277-280` on pre-main, read by the planner).

- This carries out -879 ("nothing live" on the Pi) early, and Part 2 still removes the Pi-first code (-1300 (1)).

**Kind:** correction
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1329
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-18T23:16:22Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1328, 2026-09-28-1327
**Supersedes:** -1328's conclusion "PR #261 removed the bar", and -1327's reading that the strip caused the missing search bar on List and Seasonal
**Title:** The missing search bar on List and Seasonal is not from #261: any open Journal entry hides the search bar on every tab, a rule from 2026-10-07 that is also on main. The planner's bisect compared a session with an entry open against one without (Hazel's finding; planner reproduced it)
**Observed:**
- **Hazel's probe tests through the real screen,** in landscape at 823x384, on two test-only branches:
  - List and Seasonal show the pill from a fresh start, and after the Journal with the pill hidden, on both 836916a9 and 8c90626f;
  - with a Journal entry left open, List shows **no pill on either build** (runs 39175123353 and 39175131489, with no compile errors).
  - The pill is composed only when `!journalSearchHeld` (`AvailabilityCompactScaffold.kt:1096` at 836916a9, `:1079` at 8c90626f). `journalSearchHeld` includes `isEditingJournalEntry`, with no check of the tab (`:595`).
  - Since F3 (-44), an entry stays open when you leave the Journal.
- **The planner reproduced it on the S22,** build 1.0.3472+g8c90626f, the one before #261, in landscape: Journal → New entry → List. **No search bar.**
- **Why -1328's bisect was wrong:** installing a build restarts the app, and an open entry doesn't survive a restart. So -1328's check ran with no entry open, and the owner's screenshots on 836916a9 were taken with one open. The check never saw the condition that could fail it. That is the CLAUDE.md family "a check that passes because it never saw the data that could fail it". The planner cited it as a cause without verifying the state.
- **On main:** the same rule is in production (main's `AvailabilityCompactScaffold.kt:1271`).
**What it leaves open, for the owner:**
- (a) the fix: should List and Seasonal keep their bar while a Journal entry is open, so the hide applies only on the Journal tab? Hazel has a test for it that fails today on both builds;
- (b) whether to revert #261 anyway. The revert branch is ready at fd1f9589, with no PR.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand, on branch records-after-173. The draft entry made on the S22 to reproduce this is left in place. Next free ID -1330.

**Title:** Wrong premise in the planner's go for map PR 10 (the layout): the 19 real-touch guards cannot see SightingsMap's layout; the proof is the phone (planner's slip, caught by Hazel)
**What happened:** the planner told the map helper that "the 19 real-touch guards are the key proof" for PR 10 (#315). Hazel found that every screen test puts a stub in the map slot (`AvailabilityScreenLayoutTest.kt:132`, "The tag the stub map slot carries; the real SightingsMap has no tag", and `:1062`), and the only test that composes the real slot (`MapStartGateTest`) gets the start-failure message, because MapLibre cannot load under Robolectric. So the guards prove the chrome over the map still routes touches, but cannot fail on a change to `SightingsMapLayout`. This is CLAUDE.md's "a check that passes because it never saw the data that could fail it".
**What replaced it:** the S22. For #315 (1.0.3604+g728357c7): launch check PASS; the screenshot run (16 tab changes) with an empty crash buffer; and a real adb drag across the map in portrait, before and after screenshots showing the map panned with the drag and the location dot moving with it, the chrome unchanged. **Also:** Hazel notes that the "skipped when inputs unchanged" wording in #298, #302, #307 and #310's bodies is loose in the same way #311's was (the holder is unstable, though strong skipping compares instances); left as is, as no behaviour depends on it.

**Kind:** decision
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1490
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-21T03:29:36Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1484, 2026-09-28-1487
**Title:** A standing rule for modular code (skill, CLAUDE.md line, CI warning, file ownership per dispatch); #349 merged
**Observed:**
- **#349** (2.6 D, the notice triggers): Sorrel approved after reading Compose runtime 1.12.0's flat remember/effect dispatch list; the body is byte-identical apart from the two holder edits; the suite is identical.
  - **S22:** pending-delete Undo, the trip-start warning ("Your phone is silenced…") and waypoint gone all pass; waypoint gone matches pre-main.
  - **Not reachable on the S22:** background-run (needs battery restriction), network-fixes, settings reset and the backup launch notice.
  - **Test data** deleted; Records 0.
  - Merged at 2e384d1f.
- **The planner's assessment, given when asked:** the code the maps project touches is now split. The rest of the big files is mostly order-sensitive code, comments, migrations, the camera and the Journal tab. Recommended: finish E and B+C, then split only when work needs it.
**Decision:** the owner, verbatim: "I say we can go even further: make it a skill to not couple new code, to avoid monster files, and to make it easier for coders to work in tandem. As the project grows, one coder will get overwhelmed with making several UI changes, so we need to be granular and sensible about how we code from now on." Asked four questions, they chose:
- **Where:** "Skill + CLAUDE.md line (Recommended)": a full skill beside the eight in #104, plus one line in CLAUDE.md's Building section.
- **Limits:** "Soft limits, split before adding (Recommended)": new files aim under about 400 lines; a file over about 800 must be split, as its own small PR, before new features go into it; coders say in the plan how they keep to it.
- **Enforcement:** "Warn in CI (Recommended)": a CI step that flags any PR growing a file past the limit, as a warning, not a red build. A coder builds this; it's a separate dispatch.
- **Tandem work:** "File ownership per dispatch (Recommended)": each dispatch names the files its coder may change, parallel coders never share a file, and shared files are sequenced.

The planner writes the skill (`.claude/skills/modular-code/SKILL.md`) and the CLAUDE.md pointer. The pointer is appended to an existing Building line, so no line moves (CLAUDE.md's line 253 constraint). They go to pre-main as a docs PR.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand. Next free ID -1491.

**Kind:** outcome
**ID:** 2026-09-28-1517
**Timestamp:** 2026-10-21T11:14:35Z
**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1516
**Title:** The dex register check now fails loudly on a cut-off dump (PR #360 merged into pre-main)
**Observed:**
- **Owner's go, in the planner's window:** "Yes, fix it now".
- **The change (Hazel):** only `scripts/verify-dex-register-budget.sh`. For each dex file, the dump's `Class #` record count and its complete-record count are compared against the header's class_defs_size (u32 at 0x60, after a magic check). An empty header read is also a FAIL. The FAIL line names the file and the numbers, and tells the reader to set TMPDIR to a disk-backed directory.
- **Cause, corrected by Sorrel:** the laptop's /tmp is a tmpfs mounted with usrquota, about 200 MB per user. A 400 MB write stopped at 200,384,512 bytes with rc 1. dexdump never checks its writes, so its output is cut off at the quota and it still exits 0. Free space was not the cause.
- **Proofs on pre-main e0565f31's APK:**
  - With TMPDIR on /mnt/work/scratch, the output is byte-identical to the old script's: 226,975 methods, 5 over 256.
  - With TMPDIR=/tmp, it exits 1 naming classes19.dex (12,330 records against a header of 14,660).
  - The script was restored from a saved copy, not from git.
  - CI run 39587238262 on 48fa1d75 is green and identical case by case; the nit commit bd812be4 changed only the script, which CI does not call.
- **Sorrel (Fable):** "merge after nits". Every truncation shape constructed failed loudly: a cut between records, a cut mid-record, a duplicated record, an empty dump, and dexdump failing. There was no false failure, including on a class with no source file. Nits N1, N2 and the empty-read guard were applied; N3 and N4 were skipped.
**Decision:** merged into pre-main at 86927320 (e0565f31 before, logged).
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand. Next free ID -1518.

The list reloads only at init, sweep, deletes and import, or when the Tracks chip is selected (`RecordsTab.kt:240-244`). It is old behaviour, not caused by the step-2 splits.
**Decision:**
- **The fix (planner's go):** a new `domain/TrackEnds.kt` following RecordingHalts. The service reports a track ID only after the end write succeeds; the ViewModel collects that and reloads (-1450). The race-free reasoning is in the report. TrackRecordingViewModel stays at about 922 lines with no split first, since it is a few-line fix.
- **The owner's choice:** asked whether a running recording should appear in Records, the owner chose "Only after Stop (Recommended)" over "Show it while recording". Showing a live track is a separate design.

**Continues:** 2026-09-28-1524, 2026-09-28-750
**Title:** A search from the Maps tab never moved the map (not a regression); fix it now; Clear removes the map's species chip (owner)
**Observed (Hazel's diagnosis, S22, at b1064eca):**
- **The same search on five builds:**
  - pre-main (1.0.3770), from Maps: no move;
  - main 381515c6 (1.0.3740), from Maps: no move;
  - the code of 3500 (main 19aa1058's CI debug APK, 1.0.3500), from Maps: no move;
  - #206's own head eb4932ca (1.0.3103, which brought in -750's fly-to-search), from Maps: no move;
  - pre-main, searching from List and then switching to Maps: moved.

  The device check of #206 was only a launch check (-753), so the -749 case was never re-run.
- **Cause:**
  1. The frame is applied on the map on screen, then recorded as applied in the memory above the tab (`MapDataRefresh.kt:94`).
  2. The sightings fetch sets `isLoadingSightings` (`AvailabilitySearchRuns.kt:202`), and `CompactMapTab` swaps the map for a spinner (`AvailabilityCompactMapUi.kt:348`) before the camera settles, so the saved camera is still the old one (`MapListeners.kt:189-201`).
  3. The new map restores the old camera, and `searchFrameMove` skips the already-applied frame (`MapCameraMoves.kt:83`).

  The logcat order confirms it. #336, #337 and the Phase 2 splits moved this code without changing it.
- **The species chip** ("Showing: <species> (n)") is the map's View-on-Map filter, `mapTaxonFilter` in `AvailabilityScreen.kt`. That is not -750's search selection, which Clear does reset. After Clear it reads "Showing: this species (0)".
**Decision:** the owner was asked two questions.
- **The search:** shown the step path (Maps tab → search → spinner → the map opens on the searched place at the search's zoom → leave and return: still there), they chose "Yes, fix it now (Recommended)" over the bug list.
- **The chip:** they chose "Clear removes it too (Recommended)" over keeping it.

Dispatch `prompts/preserved/2026-10-21-03.md` covers both:
- **PR A:** MapCameraMoves and MapDataRefresh only; the frame is written into the saved camera.
- **PR B:** the chip, with its route through AvailabilityScreen confirmed before building.

They come before 4a, and B and 4a run in sequence.

**Observed:**
- **What happened:** during the search-frame diagnosis, Hazel installed #206's head (1.0.3103, schema version 20) over the current build (schema version 22) with `adb install -r -d`. Debug builds add `fallbackToDestructiveMigration(true)` (`ForagerDatabase.create`), so Room deleted the database and created an empty one.
- **What was lost, on the test phone only:**
  - the recent searches;
  - a "1 unfinished entry" Journal draft of unknown origin, which was on the S22 before today's checks;
  - anything else in the database.

  Tracks, waypoints and offline regions were already empty from the checks' cleanups. The owner's real records are on their own phones, not the S22.
- **How it came to light:** Hazel's report first said no data was lost. That was corrected when the planner asked about a schema-version mismatch with the other Hazel's report (22 against 20).
- The S22 is back on 22 after #363's build was reinstalled; the 20 → 22 migrations on the empty database are inferred, not checked.
**Decision (planner):** before installing an older build on a test phone, read both builds' schema versions. Never downgrade across a schema change without asking the planner first, who brings it to the owner if the phone holds anything of theirs. This goes into every device-check dispatch from now on.
**Notes:** Written by the planner by hand. Next free ID -1527.

**Observed:** Hazel's report is docs/navigation/2026-10-21-route-cutter-phase1-report.md on route-cutter at f31ab491. Bases unmoved. Nothing was built.
- **Format, read at BRouter v1.7.10:** a cutter rewrites only the header, the touched tile indexes and the footer, and copies cells byte for byte. Its checksum is the inverse of CRC-32.
- **Where:** TypeScript modules in server/pmtiles-worker/src/rd5/ that read through a byte-range interface. The Worker can't run a JVM. One tsconfig.json line is needed.
- **Proof:** it can't run in CI unchanged; the planner confirmed ci.yml has no Node step. Hazel proposes one parallel ci.yml job of about 45 lines, using the Pi's pinned BRouter 1.7.10 jar (the planner confirmed pi-build map-build/pins.env:54-60). **Prediction (mechanism — coder), Hazel's, verbatim in substance:**
- Over a stub, every test fails on "not implemented".
- Routes that stay inside come out identical: length, cost and points.
- Removing the one-cell margin makes an edge route differ; that is the revert check.
- Under BRouter's default "dynamic range" matching, a route with an end outside the cut succeeds, snapped to the nearest way up to 60 km away. A best path that leaves the cut succeeds with a detour. A clean failure needs use_dynamic_range=0.
**Wrong premises found:**
- The dispatch's "fails cleanly … not a wrong route" is false under the default profile.
- Juniper's "position not mapped" for an outside end is the error after the dynamic retry, not the default result.
- The spike compared lengths only, not points; the planner re-read :186.
- The 10 km size prediction can't be measured by a CI fixture.
**Notes:** Privacy, raised by Juniper and Hazel: a cut on request names the area to the server. The planner read wrangler.toml:7-11: Worker logs are off because tile URLs already name the areas users look at, so a cut URL is the same exposure under the same setting (planner's reading). Written by the planner by hand. Next free ID -1546.

**Kind:** decision

**Timestamp:** 2026-10-30T04:29:43Z
**Title:** Three map asks scoped: Directions gives way to Navigate, a visible Delete for offline maps, and waypoint routes saved to the Trip Planner
**Observed:** read at pre-main 21d846b9e. Directions (the phone's maps app) is on the waypoint and trip bubbles (MapBubbleLayer.kt:144), the waypoint and trip rows (AvailabilityTripsWaypointsUi.kt:160, :300) and the details sheet (RecordDetailsContent.kt:89). Navigate exists for waypoints on the Maps tab only (MapBubbles.kt:198-202). Offline maps already delete by swiping a row, with Undo, and nothing shows it (OfflineRegionsList.kt:67). TrailRouter.route takes any start and end (TrailRouter.kt:27). A planned trip is one point and one date (PlannedTrip.kt:19).
**Decision:** the owner asked: "Waypoint to waypoint path plotting should be a thing also. In case people want to plot paths for possible trail runs." "Now that we have in-app navigation, we should remove the Google directions option from the waypoints bubble in the maps." "Also have a way to delete downloaded offline maps." Their answers:
- Directions: "Everywhere Navigate exists". Remove it wherever in-app Navigate is offered, and put Navigate where Directions is today (the lists and the details sheet). Points with no Navigate keep Directions.
